skills.name: monowatch
skills.description: Open the monowatch side panel to show Antigravity usage, including equivalent API cost, subscription payback, per-model cache hit rate, TTFT and tok/s, context window usage and compactions, subagent costs, runtime events, and model routing.

readmeMarkdown:
monowatch

A local usage dashboard for Google Antigravity, in the side panel.

English · 简体中文

## Features - **Subscription value**: see what your usage would cost at API prices, and how many times over your plan has paid for itself in the current billing cycle. - **Per-model performance**: cost, cache hit rate, time to first token and output speed for every model you use. - **Conversations, projects and CLI runs**: each one shows its cost, context usage and speed, and you can sort them by workspace. - **Conversation detail**: context window usage, compaction history, subagent costs and a per-turn breakdown. - **Local and read-only**: reads Antigravity's local data and never writes to it. No data is uploaded. - **Light / dark, English / Chinese**: follows the host theme and language automatically. ## Install ### Option 1: Let Antigravity install it (Agentic) Send this prompt to Antigravity in a chat: ```text Install https://github.com/riverxorange/agy-monowatch as a plugin, enable it, and open monowatch for me. ``` Once installed, you can mention `@[plugin:monowatch]` in any conversation (or ask Antigravity to open it) to bring up the dashboard. ### Option 2: Manual install ```bash git clone https://github.com/riverxorange/agy-monowatch.git ~/.gemini/config/plugins/monowatch ``` On Windows (PowerShell): ```powershell git clone https://github.com/riverxorange/agy-monowatch.git "$HOME\.gemini\config\plugins\monowatch" ``` Then enable **monowatch** on Antigravity's Customizations page and open it from the side panel. ## Update When a new version is available, an **Update** link appears in the panel header. You can also run `git pull` in the plugin directory. Your settings are stored separately and survive updates. ## Privacy monowatch makes one kind of network request: a version check against GitHub at most once an hour. You can turn it off in Settings. ## Development Requires only Node.js built-ins (no npm dependencies). ```bash npm --prefix sidecars/monitor_board test ``` How the data is read and calculated: [docs/TELEMETRY_SPEC.md](./docs/TELEMETRY_SPEC.md). ## License [MIT](./LICENSE). Bundled Geist fonts are licensed under the [SIL Open Font License](./sidecars/monitor_board/fonts/OFL.txt). Thanks to the [LINUX DO](https://linux.do) community. This is an unofficial community project and is not affiliated with Google.
latestReleaseNotes:
### What's New
- Added **Token Activity** heatmap on the Overview page adapting to each time window: 24-hour strip (`Today`), 7-day strip (`7d`), 7-column calendar heatmap (`Cycle` / `Month`), and GitHub-style weekly contribution grid (`All`) with hover token/cost breakdowns.
- Added **Month** (`本月`) time window alongside `Today`, `7d`, `Cycle` (or `30d`), and `All`.
- Moved **Plan** inline on the left of the Overview facts row and added a dedicated top-right **Settings** button opening a sharp-cornered modal dialog (with `Esc` and backdrop dismiss).
- Fixed two-row header layout with balanced vertical rhythm across narrow and wide panes.
